name: Jar wine
summary: Undistilled grain wine fermented with forest-leaf yeast in a jar and sipped in turns through bamboo straws. It is gently sweet, with a faint bitter edge from the yeast and the smell of fermented sticky rice.
origin: The jar wine, also called rượu ghè, of the Xơ Đăng, Ba Na, Gia Rai, Giẻ Triêng, Brâu, and other communities around Kon Tum.
culture: The jar sits at the center of the communal house at festivals. People share the straws while gongs play and the xoang is danced, and the host tops up the water after each round.
taste: Black sticky rice turns the wine red or deep purple. Sedang jar wine from Măng Đen is more fragrant and lower in alcohol, at 3–7 percent.
howToEat: Sit at one jar, let the host pour in spring water or cooled boiled water, and sip in turns. The point is to share it slowly, not to finish the jar. It belongs to harvests, Tết, new-rice meals, a new communal house, and family rites.
where: Communal houses and festivals around Kon Tum, and district markets.
seoTitle: Jar wine in Kon Tum — ruou can through straws
seoDescription: Jar wine sipped in turns through bamboo straws at the communal house, gently sweet with the smell of fermented sticky rice.
priceBand: 100,000–200,000 VND for a 5-litre jar (Go Vietnam, Kon Tum cluster); about 175,000 VND for a 4-litre container (Go Vietnam); 350,000–600,000 VND for a Sedang jar for 6–10 (Go Vietnam, Măng Đen)
